GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs shows strong fundamental health and positive trajectory. Q1 2026 was a record quarter with revenue of $17.23B (+14.4% YoY) and EPS of $17.55 (+24.3% YoY), driven by record Global Banking & Markets revenue of $12.738B (+19% YoY) and robust investment banking fees (+48% YoY). ROE reached 19.8%, up from 12.8% a year earlier, reflecting strong operating leverage. The firm's strategic pivot back to core strengths—investment banking, markets, and asset/wealth management—after exiting consumer banking is bearing fruit, with management fees in AWM growing 14% YoY and record third-party alternatives fundraising of $115B in 2025. Balance sheet is solid with $122.78B equity and CET1 at 12.5%. However, the stock has rallied significantly (+35.5% in the last quarter to $1,096.56), pushing P/E to 18.7x—near the top of its 12-month range (14.1x–18.7x)—and P/B to 2.75x, also at the high end (1.7x–2.8x). This limits upside from valuation re-rating. The upcoming Q2 2026 earnings on July 14 could serve as a near-term catalyst, though consensus expects a sequential decline (EPS $13.78 vs. Q1's $17.55) given Q1 was a record quarter. Macro backdrop is mixed: stable Fed funds rate at 3.63% and low VIX (16.78) are supportive, but rising 10-year yields (4.46%) and geopolitical risks (Iran war, oil at $80/bbl) create headwinds. News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.287 over 90 days). The SpaceX IPO underwriting ($560M in fees) and strong M&A pipeline provide near-term tailwinds, but the stock's premium valuation and cyclical earnings profile warrant a measured positive view rather than a strong conviction call.
